Subject: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification 1 Acme Health

Hi Samir / Priya 1 thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we can scope the PoC for Private/VPC deployment and validate performance SLOs.

Call summary (agreed):
- Target p95 latency for generation (end-to-end, request->first 64 tokens): <= 150ms.
- Steady-state throughput target: ~200 req/s for the LLM endpoint.
- Expected concurrency: 30-40 simultaneous streams during peak.
- Streaming: application requires token-by-token streaming (SSE/HTTP chunked) with initial-token latency <= 100ms.
- Model: opt-v2-13b (or equivalent quantized variant) for PoC; workload token lengths typically 64-512.

Private/VPC requirements discussed:
- Preferred networking: VPC peering (direct route to Redwood VPC) - primary. VPN/IPSec (TGW) as fallback.
- Egress path: need to avoid double-NAT where possible; NAT Gateways add ~15-30ms.
- Required ports: 443 (TLS) for API; 500/4500 UDP for IPSec if using VPN; allow outbound to Redwood egress IPs (will provide).
- MTU / fragmentation: MTU >=1500 recommended; please note if jumbo frames are used.
- Internal latency budget: your internal app->egress < 10ms preferred to meet p95 target.

Network checks we need from your infra team (ask them to send results back as attachments):
- traceroute/mtr from app host(s) to the Redwood egress IPs (we'll provide list).
- iperf3 test to Redwood test endpoint (we'll provide a temporary endpoint/IP).
- If possible, a sample pcap (tcpdump) of 1-2 PoC requests to capture TLS handshake timing and packet-level RTTs.

Attachments: SLO-requirements.pdf (high level targets + test plan).

Concrete next steps / timeline:
1) We’ll provision a PoC endpoint in your preferred region and send the egress IPs + iperf target by EOD today. (Owner: Jordan)
2) Acme infra runs traceroute/iperf + captures pcap and returns results. Please include typical pod-to-egress latency and NAT info. (Owner: Acme)
3) Redwood will run an initial synthetic run to validate latency/throughput and share a short report. If numbers exceed targets, we’ll iterate on placement/routing and recommend configuration (keepalives, TCP tuning, batching knobs). (Owner: Marissa/Jordan)

PoC window: Prefer next-week test window (Mon-Wed) - can you confirm availability?

Thanks - cc’ing Jordan and Aditya to track infra setup.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Samir - great, thanks for the quick tests and the pcap. A few clarifications and our PoC logistics: 

1) IPs & iperf endpoint: Jordan - can you confirm the temporary iperf3/TCP endpoint and list of Redwood egress IPs we should share?

2) Minimum tests we need from Acme infra before the PoC run:
   - iperf3 (TCP and UDP) from a representative app host to the provided endpoint for 60s (report throughput and jitter).
   - traceroute/mtr + tcpdump capturing TLS handshake timing for a few sessions. The pcap you sent is helpful - we’ll look for SYN->TLS-handshake->first-payload timing.
   - If TGW peering is an option, please prioritize that over NAT for the PoC (we’ll still accept NAT results but expect ~15-25ms added).

3) Config suggestions from Redwood side:
   - Prefer VPC peering + static route to avoid NAT.
   - Ensure TCP keepalives (60s) and lower initial congestion window if you see bursty packet loss - we’ll advise based on pcap.
   - For streaming we’ll negotiate chunk sizes; in PoC we’ll push a stream with 1-8 token flushes to validate initial-token latencies.

4) PoC run: Tuesday 09:00-12:00 PDT works. Jordan & I will be available to run synthetic load and walk through packet captures live. If peering isn’t ready, we’ll run over your NAT and include the difference in the report.

Next actions:
- Jordan to share endpoints/IPs (today EOD).
- Acme to run iperf/traceroute/tcpdump and upload results (Samir).
- Redwood to provision PoC and run synthetic tests on Tue.

Thanks - looking forward.

--
Marissa
